modern: In the writings of the Ephesians there was this rule: to think constantly of one of the men of former times who practised virtue.
original: In the writings of the [Ephesians] there was this precept, constantly to think of some one of the men of former times who practiced virtue.

explained.summary: Marcus notes an old rule from some writings from Ephesus: keep constantly in mind someone from the past who lived a good life. Having a model to measure yourself against makes virtue concrete and gives you someone to ask, in effect, what would they do here.
explained.today: That might be a grandparent who stayed kind through hard times, a teacher who was always fair, or a figure from history you admire. Picturing how they’d handle the tense meeting or the family row is a quick way to find your better self.
